messages:
maya: quick question - we merged an internal startup-order change that doesn't change public APIs but could surface flakes in a few services. do we bump patch or keep same tag?
felix: if there's any possibility teams need to rollback explicitly, bump patch. patch = rollback surface.
sanjay: +1. but let's be precise about tagging so automation and backports don't break. we rely on numeric-only tags in backport tooling.
ryan: thought: use buildmeta like `v1.4.2+infra1` to convey infra context? keeps semver precedence but gives info.
maya: hm buildmeta is ignored for precedence per semver; also `git describe` ordering might not follow same semantics. could confuse release tools.
felix: pre-release suffixes (`-infra.1`) affect ordering too and break our backport scripts. i vote for numeric-only tags for releases.
sanjay: pragmatic rule proposal: 1) always bump patch for any change that might require a manual rollback 2) keep tags as `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` numeric-only 3) put infra context in release body + `deploy` labels (e.g., `rollback-candidate:true`) 4) add a short compat-risk line in release notes: low/med/high
maya: i like that. keeps tooling simple and gives ops info where they look (release notes, deploy UI). i'll update the release playbook.
ryan: can deploy-bot attach labels automatically? e.g., when PR touches `runtime/*` or `bin/startup` add `rollback-candidate` on canary deploys.
deploy-bot: deploy request received: check:canary v1.4.2 -> starting rollout (cmd: `/deploy v1.4.2 --canary 5% --window 15m`); labels: rollback-candidate:true; note: compat-risk=medium
sanjay: perfect. one more: add an on-call checklist in the release body: last-good-tag, rollback command (`/deploy <last-good-tag> --force`), monitoring links, expected noisy metrics.
maya: i'll add a small helper that auto-prepares that checklist from PR metadata. also will add a short line to release notes template: "compat-risk: low/medium/high" and "rollback-candidate: true/false".
felix: sounds good. final ask: ensure backport bot ignores non-numeric suffixes and errors loudly if someone tries to create `v1.4.2-infra.1`. enforce via branch protection + CI check.
ryan: agree, add CI lint to fail tag patterns that don't match `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`.
maya: will follow up with a tiny RFC doc and drop a link here when done. thanks :thumbsup:
